# FluffelDrone v1 Brushed – devlog

> A drone with a custom PCB: Microcontroller: ESP32-CAM (acting as flight controller, Wi-Fi receiver for MQTT control, and video streamer). IMU/Sensor: MPU6050 (placed directly in the geometric center of the board). Power: 1S LiPo Battery (3.7V - 4.2V), stepped down via an TPS63070 voltage regulator for the ICs. Motors: 4x 8520 coreless brushed motors, driven by SI2302 N-Channel MOSFETs with 1N4148 flyback/protection diodes parallel to each motor. Control: Controlled via Python/MQTT over Wi-Fi. Mounting: No mounting holes because the frame will be 3D printed and the board will be glued to save weight.

## Design

# October 2, 2026: First version of the PCB.
<!-- fabricate:entry 97 -->

I have spent 6 hours so far working on my first custom micro drone project, 'FluffelDrone'. During this time, I have successfully accomplished the following milestones:
• Schematic Design: Created a complete 1S LiPo-powered circuit diagram in EasyEDA. It integrates an ESP32-CAM module, an MPU6050 IMU sensor, an AMS1117-3.3V voltage regulator, and four SI2302 N-Channel MOSFETs with protective 1N4148 flyback diodes for the motors.
• Component Placement: Arranged the components on a custom 50x50 mm 2-layer PCB layout, ensuring the MPU6050 sensor sits perfectly in the geometric center of the board for ideal flight stabilization.
• Routing & DRC Verification: Fixed initial clearance errors by utilizing the EasyEDA Auto-Router with customized net rules. Main power traces were widened to 0.8mm - 1.0mm to handle the high motor current. A solid GND copper pour was applied to the bottom layer, and the project now successfully passes the Design Rule Check (DRC) with 0 errors.
